en: Theragāthā 1.88 Ekakanipāta Navamavagga The Elder’s Verses 1.88, Chapter Nine, Section on Single Verses (Ekakanipāta) I have crossed over the flood; I am free from fear. Having reached the further shore, I dwell in peace. My mind is well-liberated; I am one who has attained Nibbāna. I am a sage, a tamed one, one who has done his task. I am a bhikkhu who has lived the holy life. I am one who has reached the goal. I am a bhikkhu who has done what was to be done. I am a bhikkhu who has laid down the burden. I am a bhikkhu whose tethers are cut. I am a bhikkhu who has no more future existence. I am a bhikkhu who has reached the end of suffering. I am a bhikkhu who has attained the destruction of the taints. I am a bhikkhu who has realized the supreme security from bondage. I am a bhikkhu who has attained the unsurpassed bliss of liberation.
